answer: Work waits on the cipher until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the velvet of the next round. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, forfeited on duplicate submission, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the horizon of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
